body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-09. Credit: CWNG NEW2 caught the outbound half; the inbound half was
caught independently the same day. Both are the same defect.

The 2026-08-05 tracker migration (#1391) moved self-filed issues into the findings
ledger. It did not preserve DELIVERY state in either direction, and the resulting
records are indistinguishable at a glance from records that mean the opposite.

OUTBOUND — a closed issue that never shipped:
  #871 "New UI: Duplicate action for ordinary shelves" is CLOSED (2026-08-05). Its
  closing comment says it moved to the ledger (F-d60c09). It was NOT delivered:
  `Duplicate` appears nowhere in Shelf.tsx or Shelves.tsx, and useDuplicateMagicShelf
  is the only duplicate action in the frontend. Ordinary shelves still cannot be
  duplicated.

INBOUND — an open finding that had already shipped:
  F-c78e8c was migrated from #870 on 2026-08-05 with status "open". The fix had landed
  2026-07-20 (f74c280fe, v4.1.19) — 16 days earlier. Stale on arrival. Resolved in
  #1489.

WHY IT MATTERS: anyone reconciling "what shipped" against issue state will
over-report, and anyone reconciling against ledger state will under-report. It already
happened: counting #867's five items off issue state gave "two of five shipped" when
the verified answer is ONE of five (only #870). The wrong count was caught before it
reached a user, but it was one message away from being told to the reporter.

Both dates are 2026-08-05, so the blast radius is bounded to that migration batch.

REMEDY, in order of value:
1. Audit the #1391 batch. For every issue closed on 2026-08-05 with a
   migrated-to-ledger comment, check the CODE for delivery and correct whichever side
   is wrong — close the finding if it shipped, or note non-delivery on the issue if it
   did not.
2. Make the two states distinguishable going forward. A migrated-not-delivered issue
   should carry a label (e.g. `migrated-to-ledger`) so it is not silently counted as
   delivered by anything reading issue state.
3. Never derive "did this ship" from issue state alone in this repo. Check the tree.
   That is what caught both halves here.

RELATED: F-c78e8c (the inbound instance), F-d60c09 (the outbound one), #867
(the umbrella whose count was wrong), #1489.
title: Issues closed by the #1391 migration read as shipped; findings migrated from them read as open
